_meta.indication: VYZULTA is a prostaglandin analog indicated for the reduction of intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.
_meta.receipt_date: July 21, 2015 (NDA dated and received July 21, 2015); resubmission (complete response) received August 17, 2017

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-masked, randomized, active-controlled, parallel-group efficacy phase (3 months) with an open-label safety extension phase (9 months); control was timolol maleate 0.5% BID
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension with baseline IOP approximately 25-27 mmHg
pivotal_trials.endpoint: IOP at 8AM, 12PM and 4PM at Visit 4 (Week 2), Visit 5 (Week 6) and Visit 6 (Month 3)
pivotal_trials.n: 417 subjects analyzed (latanoprostene 0.024% 286 patients; timolol 0.5% BID 134 patients)
pivotal_trials.result: IOP lowering for latanoprostene was approximately 7-9 mmHg and for timolol approximately 6-8 mmHg at each time point; difference in mean IOP <1.5 mmHg at all time points and <1 mmHg at the majority of time points, meeting the non-inferiority criteria

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-masked, randomized, active-controlled, parallel-group efficacy phase (3 months) with an open-label safety extension phase (3 months); control was timolol maleate 0.5% BID
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension with baseline IOP approximately 25-27 mmHg
pivotal_trials.endpoint: IOP at 8AM, 12PM and 4PM at Visit 4 (Week 2), Visit 5 (Week 6) and Visit 6 (Month 3)
pivotal_trials.n: 420 randomized subjects (latanoprostene 0.024% 283 patients; timolol 0.5% BID 137 patients)
pivotal_trials.result: IOP lowering for latanoprostene was approximately 7-9 mmHg and for timolol approximately 6-8 mmHg at each time point; the mean IOP difference and upper CI were within 1 mmHg at all time points and within 1.5 mmHg at all time points, meeting non-inferiority

key_safety: The most common ocular adverse events were conjunctival/ocular hyperemia (10%) and eye irritation (5%); the most common nonocular adverse event was nasopharyngitis (5%). The most significant long-term adverse events are expected to be related to increases in pigmentation.
target_moa: Latanoprostene bunod lowers IOP by increasing outflow of aqueous humor through both the trabecular meshwork and uveoscleral routes; it is metabolized to latanoprost acid (a prostaglandin F2-alpha receptor agonist) and butanediol mononitrate, which is metabolized to nitric oxide.
modality: Small molecule (prostaglandin analogue / F2-alpha receptor agonist, nitric oxide-donating)

summary.text: Vyzulta was approved under a standard 505(b) NDA supported by two adequate and well-controlled non-inferiority trials (#769 and #770) versus timolol; no expedited-program designations are documented. Approval followed two prior Complete Response letters (July 21, 2016 and August 7, 2017) related to GMP manufacturing-facility deficiencies, which were resolved before approval.

citations.quote: The safety and efficacy of the proposed drug product was supported by two adequate and well controlled studies in patients with elevated intraocular pressure. The control group in each study was timolol ophthalmic solution, 0.5% administered twice daily (BID).

The original NDA was submitted on July 21, 2015. Complete Response (CR) letters dated July 21, 2016, and August 7, 2017, were issued. The Applicant has addressed the deficiency identified in the CR regarding the good manufacturing practice (GMP) status of the manufacturing facility in this submiss

basis.text: The CRLs cited a manufacturing deficiency: GMP deficiencies observed at the Bausch & Lomb drug product manufacturing facility required satisfactory resolution before the application could be approved.
